vulnerability_analysis: The sendBNBToAdmin function uses transfer() without checking the return value. In Solidity 0.6.12, transfer() returns false on failure instead of reverting. If the admin wallet is a contract that reverts on receive, the transfer will fail silently, leaving ETH stuck in the contract. An attacker who controls the admin wallet can: 1) Set admin to a reverting contract, 2) Trigger swapAndLiquify to accumulate stuck ETH, 3) Change admin to their EOA address, 4) Trigger swapAndLiquify again to receive the accumulated ETH.
attack_strategy: 1. Become owner of the contract via storage manipulation. 2. Deploy a malicious admin contract that reverts in receive(). 3. Set admin to the malicious contract. 4. Accumulate fee tokens in the contract by making transfers. 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify - ETH gets stuck. 6. Change admin to attacker's EOA. 7. Trigger swapAndLiquify again - stuck ETH is sent to attacker.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store to overwrite the owner slot and become owner. 2. Deploy RevertingAdmin contract. 3. Call _setReceiverWallet to set admin to RevertingAdmin. 4. Get JizzJet tokens via deal(). 5. Make transfers to generate fee tokens in contract. 6. Trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring from a non-pair address when contract has enough tokens. 7. Verify ETH is stuck in contract. 8. Change admin to attacker EOA. 9. Accumulate more fees and trigger swapAndLiquify again. 10. Verify attacker's ETH balance increased.
